reason: The hypothesis directly combines the specific finding from P4 (a gradient HfZr alloy layer improves adhesion in a VZrHfNbTa coating) with the demonstrated benefit of Y and Hf co-doping in reducing scale spallation in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 coatings under identical hot corrosion conditions (P3, P5). It proposes applying this combined approach—a deliberate Hf-rich interlayer to form a graded Hf-Zr interface—to a generic HEA bond coat, which is a synthesis of two separate results into one new proposal.
copied_elements: Hf-rich interlayer in HEA bond coat
mechanism: Hf diffusion and reaction with Zr to form gradient layer
predicted outcome: reduced oxide scale spallation and improved adhesion
